The '''2020–21 Czech First League''', known as the '''[[Czech First League|Fortuna liga]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 28th season of the [[Czech Republic]]'s top-tier [[association football|football]] for professional clubs since its establishment in 1993. [[Slavia Prague]] have won their twenty-first league title which was their fourth in the last five years. The season was initially scheduled to start on 11 July <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/382375/fortuna-liga-program-sezony-a-terminy-prvnich-kol-vcetne-prenosu.html|title=FORTUNA:LIGA: program sezony a termíny prvních kol včetně přenosů|website=iSport.cz}}</ref> but was delayed until 21 August as a consequence of the postponement of the previous season's conclusion due to the outbreak of [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic|COVID-19]]. The first half of the season only had 15 rounds and finished on 19 December, while the spring half commenced on 29 January 2021, the earliest such date in league history.

This season was set to be played with 18 clubs, each team played in the league format with home and away matches, and the bottom three teams were relegated directly to the second league at the end of the season. It was the third season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]], featuring it in six to eight matches per match-week in the first half of the season. From January 2021, all nine matches had VAR.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/382987/novinky-a-chytaky-v-pravidlech-fotbalu-kdy-se-piska-ruka-a-ofsajd.html|title=Novinky a "chytáky" v pravidlech fotbalu: kdy se píská ruka a ofsajd?|website=iSport.cz}}</ref> As was the case at the end of the previous season, there will be limited attendance from the fans in the stadiums due to measures related to COVID-19 pandemic.

==Summary==

This season was the third to have betting agency [[Fortuna (betting)|Fortuna]] as the title sponsor. In February 2020 the sponsorship contract was extended by another two years to expire in 2023–24.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lfafotbal.cz/clanek/207-fortuna-prodlouzila-kontrakt-s-lfa-do-roku-2024|title=Fortuna prodloužila kontrakt s LFA do roku 2024|website=Ligová fotbalová asociace}}</ref> It was also the third season with TV broadcasting rights held by O2 TV, showing all nine matches per match-week. Further, the national broadcaster [[ČT Sport]] broadcast one match per round (fourth option) and the newspaper [[iSport.cz]] holds rights for the highlights from all matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/fotbalova-liga-o2-tv-fortuna-liga-prenosy.A180618_171315_fotbal_min|title=Fotbalová liga na placeném kanále, O2 TV získala práva na čtyři roky|date=18 June 2018|website=iDNES.cz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mediaguru.cz/clanky/2019/07/fotbalovou-ligu-opet-prinese-hlavne-o2-tv-cast-i-ct/|title=Fotbalovou ligu opět přinese hlavně O2 TV, část i ČT|website=MediaGuru.cz}}</ref>

With [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia]], [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria]], and [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta]] finishing top-three in the [[2019–20 Czech First League|2019–20 season]], many expected a close race for the title amongst this trio. Sparta and Slavia started the season in strong form with unbeaten runs in their first six matches, while Viktoria lost in the second round in [[FC Slovan Liberec|Liberec]]. The season was postponed in October due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic|COVID-19]] measures with Sparta at the top, followed by Slavia and Viktoria. The race for the title resumed behind closed doors in November with Viktoria's 3–1 win over Sparta in the seventh round and opened up a lead for the rivals Slavia. Sparta and Viktoria suffered another loss in the following round and the gap increased. Slavia maintained their lead for the remainder of the season.

The last match of the autumn program was played on 23 December, the latest such date in Czech league history. Before the four-week winter break, Slavia held a 7-point lead ahead of Sparta and [[FK Jablonec|Jablonec]]. At the other end of the table [[FC Zbrojovka Brno|Brno]], [[1. FK Příbram|Příbram]], and [[SFC Opava|Opava]] were positioned in the relegation zone. Due to several teams having troubles with the COVID-19 during and after the break, the schedule was condensed and an updated league calendar was issued. Mid-week slots were added and the league continued to be played in such format until the end of the season. 

After February's match-week 17 Sparta's 0–1 loss against [[Bohemians 1905|Bohemians]], their coach [[Václav Kotal]] was sacked and replaced with three-time league champion and former [[Czech Republic national football team|national team]] coach, [[Pavel Vrba]], who won his first game in charge against [[SK Sigma Olomouc|Olomouc]], 2–3 away.

During the season, Slavia broke several Czech League all-time records. They achieved a record 41 consecutive matches unbeaten with a draw at Bohemians on 24 April 2021 <ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.slavia.cz/clanek.asp?id=18362|title=75 let starý rekord pokořen: 41 utkání bez prohry|date=26 April 2021|website=www.slavia.cz}}</ref> and increased it to 46 on the last matchday (the run still continues) to finish the whole season with an unbeaten record. Slavia recorded 24 wins, 86 points, and 85 goals scored in a single season, which are season records for the Czech first league.

On 2 May 2021, Sparta drew 2–2 in Liberec, mathematically confirming Slavia as champions for the third successive season. Slavia defeated Viktoria 5–1 in [[Sinobo Stadium]] later that evening. Viktoria, positioned 5th, drew the next fixture with Příbram 3–3, and following the match, coach [[Adrián Guľa|Guľa]] was sacked.<ref name="isport.blesk.cz">{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/395907/plzen-po-blamazi-s-pribrami-odvolala-gulu-nastupce-na-zacatku-tydne.html |title=Plzeň po blamáži s Příbramí odvolala Guľu! Nástupce na začátku týdne |date=9 May 2021|website=blesk.cz}}</ref>

On 8 May 2021, Opava was confirmed to be the first team to be relegated to the [[Czech National Football League|FNL]] after a 1–1 draw at [[FC Fastav Zlín|Zlín]], with three games remaining ending their three-year tenure in the first league.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/395865/video-zlin-opava-1-1-slezane-jsou-prvnim-sestupujicim-do-druhe-ligy.html|title=Slezané jsou prvním sestupujícím do druhé ligy|date=8 May 2021|website=www.isport.blesk.cz}}</ref> A week later on 16 May 2021, 15th-placed [[FK Teplice|Teplice]] defeated [[Dynamo České Budějovice|České Budějovice]] and relegated Brno, immediately returning to the FNL after a season's presence in the top flight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/396276/video-teplice-c-budejovice-2-0-vyhra-domacich-rozhodla-o-sestupu-brna.html|title=Teplice - Č. Budějovice 2:0. Výhra domácích rozhodla o sestupu Brna|date=16 May 2021|website=www.slavia.cz}}</ref> On 23 May 2021, Příbram was the third and final team to be relegated following a 0–1 defeat at home against Pardubice with one game remaining, also ending their First League tenure after three-years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/sport/fotbal/rozhodnuto-sestupuje-take-starkova-pribram-dekujeme-pardubicim-my-byli-strasni-zlobil-se-kouc-teplic.A210523_192351_ln-sport-fotbal_livs|title=Rozhodnuto, sestupuje také Starkova Příbram.|date=23 May 2021|website=www.lidovky.cz}}</ref>

===Teams relegated from Czech First League===
In the last season's format of the league, all teams played a round-robin home and away format of the league. After 30 matches the teams were divided into championship (top 6), play-off (7th–10th), and relegation (bottom 6) groups. Points and goals in the relegation group were fully carried over from the regular season. The last team should have been relegated and the two teams positioned 14th and 15th should have played a playoff format with second league teams positioned second and third. The relegation group was scheduled to conclude on 7 July 2020 but as a result of three Karviná players tested positive for COVID-19, the final two rounds of matches were postponed to 23 and 26 July.<ref>{{cite web |title=Karvinští fotbalisté jsou zdraví, dohrání ligy nic nebrání|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/karvina-koronavirus-testy-negativni.A200715_205336_fotbal_rou?|publisher=iDnes|language=cs|date=2020-07-15}}</ref> On 23 July, the date of the first postponed round, one player from Opava tested positive and the team was placed into two weeks long isolation which led to the abandonment of the last two rounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/sport/fotbal/fotbal-fortuna-liga-koronavirus-nakaza-karantena-opava-skupina-o-udrzeni-sestup_2007231218_tat|title=Další komplikace pro fotbalovou ligu. Opava hlásí nákazu koronavirem a jde do karantény|website=iROZHLAS|language=cs|date=2020-07-23}}</ref>

On 24 July the league FA announced that due to time pressure, the relegation group would remain unfinished and as a consequence, no team could be relegated. To avoid playing the 2020–21 season with an odd number of teams, automatic promotion was extended to the second-placed team as well as the winners of the Second League. The elimination play-offs were cancelled and the number of participants for the 2020–21 season increased from 16 to 18.

At the end of the regular season, [[1. FK Příbram]] were in last position, with elimination playoff spots held by [[MFK Karviná]] and [[SFC Opava]]. The same order was recorded after playing three rounds of the relegation group.

=== Teams promoted to Czech First League ===

The [[2019–20 Czech National Football League|second league]] was also impacted by COVID pandemic but fully finished after a delay. On 11 July 2020 in the penultimate round of the season [[FK Pardubice]] beat [[FC Slavoj Vyšehrad|Vyšehrad]] 4–1 and secured automatic promotion to the First League for the first time in their history. Pardubice were previously represented three times in the [[Czechoslovak First League]], by another team from the city, most recently in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/domaci-souteze/fk-pardubice-historie-prvni-liga-druha-liga-fotbal.A200716_559531_fot_dsouteze_elv|title=Pardubice počtvrté mezi elitou. Na postup do první ligy čekaly přes půl století|date=16 July 2020|website=iDNES.cz}}</ref>

Since the decision that all sixteen teams would remain in the top league and to prevent having an odd number of participants, the second place holder [[FC Zbrojovka Brno|Brno]] was invited to join the top tier after an absence of two years. Third-placed team [[FK Dukla Prague|Dukla Prague]] remained in the second league without the right to play a playoff match.

=== Locations and stadiums ===

The home stadium of newly promoted FK Pardubice was not certified by the league to host the First League matches. The club opted to play their home league matches at Bohemians' [[Ďolíček]] stadium.<ref name="pardubice-stadium-20">{{cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/fk-pardubice-stadion-domaci-zapasy-bohemians-1905.A200804_182921_fotbal_min|title=Pardubice si vybraly. Na stadionu Bohemians budou hrát ligu dva kluby|language=cs|work=idnes.cz|date=4 August 2020|access-date=5 August 2020}}</ref>
